result.message:
Fix hexbin mincnt inconsistency when C is supplied (issue: "Inconsistent behavior of hexbins mincnt parameter, depending on C parameter").

Root cause: in Axes.hexbin, the C-is-None branch keeps a bin when it holds at least mincnt points (accum < mincnt -> NaN drops it), while the C-supplied branch used `len(acc) > mincnt`, dropping bins holding exactly mincnt points.

Change: lib/matplotlib/axes/_axes.py — in the C-supplied accumulation, `reduce_C_function(acc) if len(acc) > mincnt else np.nan` becomes `len(acc) >= mincnt`, matching the requested resolution and making mincnt consistent in both paths (a bin is dropped only when it contains fewer than mincnt points).

Regression test: lib/matplotlib/tests/test_axes.py — test_hexbin_mincnt_behavior asserts that with mincnt=2 no single-count bin survives, both without C (counts path) and with C + reduce_C_function=np.sum.

Verification (current version v3, fixed candidate patch-1): public pytest on lib/matplotlib/tests/test_axes.py -k hexbin -> 8 collected, 8 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors. Same-version public evidence only; not official acceptance.

Public pytest hexbin scope on the delivered v3: 8 passed. patch-1 published; delivery-1 submitted.
